conventions.commits: Conventional commits (feat, chore, ci, docs, security)
conventions.testing: Unit tests in #[cfg(test)] modules, uses tree-sitter parser for verification
conventions.linting: clippy with deny for undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used
conventions.error_handling: Uses thiserror for error types, Option/Result patterns

patterns: Language-specific handler file with query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, etc.)
Registration in mod.rs get_language_info() and get_ts_language() match arms
constraints: DEFUSE_QUERY is mandatory (LanguageInfo.defuse_query is Option<&'static str>)
tree-sitter-swift 0.7.3 normal dependency is tree-sitter-language ^0.1.0 only
No feature flags for language registration (all languages unconditionally compiled)
Must follow existing pattern: mod swift; in mod.rs, swift in get_language_info/get_ts_language
test_coverage: Each language handler has #[cfg(test)] module with tests for query validation, extraction functions, and semantic analysis integration. Java has 8+ tests covering element extraction, inheritance, and defuse sites.

library_findings.notes: Normal dep: tree-sitter-language ^0.1.0; dev dep: tree-sitter (no conflict with workspace 0.26.13)

approaches.name: Full Java-style implementation
approaches.description: Create swift.rs with all query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY) and handlers (extract_function_name, find_receiver_type, extract_inheritance). Model after java.rs.
pros: Complete feature parity with other languages

approaches.name: Minimal CSS-style implementation
approaches.description: Create swift.rs with only ELEMENT_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY. Set DEFUSE_QUERY to None, handlers to None. Follow css.rs pattern.

approaches.name: Hybrid Swift-optimized implementation
approaches.description: Implement ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, and DEFUSE_QUERY. Skip extract_function_name/find_receiver_type (use None). Implement extract_inheritance for class_declaration/protocol_declaration. Use declaration_kind field to distinguish struct/enum/extension.
pros: Handles all declaration kinds via class_declaration
cons: Requires understanding Swift grammar node types

recommendation: Approach 3 (Hybrid Swift-optimized). The issue explicitly requires DEFUSE_QUERY and extract_inheritance. Swift's class_declaration node with declaration_kind field elegantly handles class/struct/actor/enum/extension/protocol. This approach provides full functionality without unnecessary handlers.
